features.method: OpenStreetMap way 370719333 (building, ref '53-0003', whose source tag is the LANL report LA-UR-05-9402) used verbatim: a straight, stepped-edge structure 695 m long and 26 m wide (area 7 596 m2) running east-west along the mesa and ending at the main LANSCE hall. Why it is drawn as the linac: LANL says the linac 'stretch[es] eastward from the Laboratory along a narrow mesa top' (src:lanl-geo-lansce-science-2006); the ref 53-0003 is the same TA-53 building number as the county Structures layer's 'Los Alamos Neutron Science Cen' (BLDG_ID 3), whose outline (the main hall, 233 m across) is adjoined by this structure's east end; and no other structure of that length exists at TA-53. No fetched source says in so many words that building 53-3 holds the linac, so confidence stays approximate. Length: LANL's linac page says 'The third and longest stage of the accelerator (800m) is the side-coupled-cavity linac' (src:geo-lanl-linac-page); the outline is 695 m, a building against an accelerator stage, so no check row is written; the 105 m difference is recorded as a conflict in the worklog.
features.name: LANSCE linac structure (TA-53 building 53-0003, long east-west wing)

provenance.locator: OSM way/370719333 version 4 (2026-01-06T03:06:46Z) fetched 2026-10-25T11:26:26Z; LA-UR-05-9402 first paragraph (linac 'stretching eastward ... along a narrow mesa top'); county Structures layer BLDG_ID 3
provenance.note: The outline is the surface structure, not a surveyed beam axis; identity rests on the building number, direction and length, not on a source that says 'the linac is building 53-3'.

summary.plain: The LANSCE accelerator site (Technical Area 53, the Meson Physics Facility) at Los Alamos National Laboratory, New Mexico: the 695 m building along the mesa top that houses the 800 MeV proton linac, the main hall, the Proton Storage Ring building (a 32 m circle) and the Lujan Center, with the technical-area boundary and the other buildings. Positions come from OpenStreetMap and Los Alamos County map data, not from a survey.

unlocated.backlog: Find a LANSCE/LAMPF-era civil-engineering drawing or the original LSND proposal's site plan giving Line A's/Area A's beamline heading and the A6 beam stop's coordinates or its distance and bearing from a surveyed LANSCE control point.
unlocated.reason: LSND's own NIM paper places it about 30 m from the A6 proton beam stop (src:lsnd-nim-1997-detector-paper), and a separate 2020 paper on LANSCE's Area A places a (different, later-proposed) target 'near the center of Area A, some 100 m downstream of the end of the 800-MeV accelerator' (src:geo-lanl-fpns-area-a-nim-2020) -- but the 800-MeV accelerator's own end point is not itself located this session (see accelerator:lansce, above), and no source gives the switchyard/Line-A bend's heading, so a derived point would rest on an unsourced direction, not a sourced one. LSND is therefore left undrawn rather than guessed; the detector-hosting site itself (site:lanl-lansce) is drawn. Release pass 2026-10-25: the county layer has a 'Neutrion Exper Service Bl' (building 364, drawn as a context building) at LANSCE, but nothing fetched says it belongs to LSND or where the A6 beam stop is, so LSND is still not placed.
